subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of electric current?
questions.explain: Electric current is measured in amperes (amps), where one amp is one coulomb of charge flowing per second.

questions.q: In the equation Q = I × t, what does the quantity Q represent, and in what unit is it measured?
questions.explain: Q is the charge in coulombs, equal to the current (amps) multiplied by the time (seconds).

questions.q: What is the unit of electrical resistance?
questions.explain: Resistance is measured in ohms (Ω), defined by the equation V = I × R.

questions.q: The equation linking potential difference, current and resistance is V = I × R. Rearranged to make resistance the subject, this becomes:
questions.explain: Dividing potential difference by current gives resistance, so R = V ÷ I.

questions.q: For an ohmic conductor kept at constant temperature, what does the current–potential difference (I–V) graph look like?
options: A straight line through the origin
A curve that becomes less steep as pd increases
A curve that only allows current in one direction
questions.explain: An ohmic conductor at constant temperature has constant resistance, so current is directly proportional to potential difference, giving a straight line through the origin.

questions.q: As the current through a filament lamp increases, what happens to the resistance of the filament?
options: It increases because the filament gets hotter
It stays constant at all currents
It decreases because the filament gets hotter
It falls to zero once the lamp lights
questions.explain: Higher current heats the filament, making the metal ions vibrate more and impede electron flow, so resistance increases.

questions.q: How does the resistance of a thermistor change as its temperature rises?
questions.explain: A thermistor's resistance decreases as temperature increases, which makes it useful in temperature-sensing circuits.

questions.q: A current of 2 A flows through a resistor of resistance 6 Ω. What is the potential difference across the resistor?
questions.explain: Using V = I × R gives V = 2 × 6 = 12 V.

questions.q: In a series circuit, how does the current compare at different points around the circuit?
options: The current is the same at every point
The current is largest nearest the cell
The current is shared between components
The current is zero except across the cell
questions.explain: In a series circuit there is only one path, so the same current flows through every component.

questions.q: Two identical lamps are connected in parallel across a battery. How does the potential difference across each lamp compare with the battery's potential difference?
options: Each lamp has the full battery potential difference across it
Each lamp has half the battery potential difference
The potential difference across the lamps adds up to twice the battery's
The potential difference depends on the current through each lamp
questions.explain: Components in parallel are connected across the same two points, so each branch has the full supply potential difference.

questions.q: How is the total resistance of two resistors connected in series found?
options: Take the smaller of the two resistances
The total is less than either resistance
questions.explain: In series the resistances simply add, so the total resistance is greater than either individual resistor.

questions.q: When two resistors are connected in parallel, how does the total resistance compare with the individual resistances?
options: It is less than the smaller of the two resistances
It equals the sum of the two resistances
It equals the average of the two resistances
It is greater than the larger of the two resistances
questions.explain: Adding a parallel path provides more routes for current, so the total resistance is lower than either individual resistor.

questions.q: A 4 Ω resistor and a 6 Ω resistor are connected in series. What is the total resistance of the combination?
questions.explain: Series resistances add, so the total is 4 + 6 = 10 Ω.

questions.q: What are the voltage and frequency of the UK mains electricity supply?
questions.explain: UK mains is an alternating current (a.c.) supply of about 230 V with a frequency of 50 Hz.

questions.q: In a UK three-core mains cable, what is the colour of the insulation on the live wire?
questions.explain: The live wire is insulated in brown, the neutral in blue, and the earth in green-and-yellow stripes.

questions.q: What are the colours of the insulation on the earth wire in a UK mains plug?
questions.explain: The earth wire is identified by green-and-yellow striped insulation.

questions.q: Why is a fuse fitted in the live wire of an appliance rather than the neutral wire?
options: So that when it melts it disconnects the appliance from the dangerous live supply
Because the neutral wire carries no current
Because fuses only work at high voltages
So that the appliance keeps working after the fuse melts
questions.explain: Placing the fuse in the live wire means that when it melts the appliance is isolated from the high-potential live supply, making it safe.

questions.q: An appliance is described as being 'double insulated'. What does this mean for its wiring?
options: It has a plastic casing and needs no earth wire
It must always be connected using an earth wire
It uses two live wires for extra power
It has no fuse in its plug
questions.explain: Double-insulated appliances have a non-conductive (plastic) casing that cannot become live, so no earth wire is required.

questions.q: Which equation correctly gives the electrical power transferred by a component?
questions.explain: Electrical power equals current multiplied by potential difference, P = I × V (also written P = I²R or P = V²/R).

questions.q: A 100 W lamp is switched on for 60 seconds. How much energy is transferred, using E = P × t?
questions.explain: Energy transferred E = P × t = 100 × 60 = 6000 J.
